**Continuous 2.16.0**, a community-maintained fork of the Continue VS Code extension. Continuous is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or supported by Continue Dev, Inc.

It installs alongside the original extension (its ID is `b1tninja.continuous`), brings your existing `~/.continue` configuration with it, and collects no telemetry. To update from 2.14.0, 2.12.x, 2.10.x or 2.4.x, install the new `.vsix` the same way, or let the Marketplace update it. Coming from 2.4.1 or earlier, also see [Continued is now Continuous](https://github.com/b1tninja/continuous/releases/tag/v2.4.2-vscode) in the 2.4.2 notes: the extension ID changed.

## Install

1. Download the `.vsix` for your platform below and, optionally, check it against `SHA256SUMS.txt`.
2. Run `code --install-extension continuous-<platform>-2.16.0.vsix --force`, or in VS Code use the Extensions view: `...` → **Install from VSIX…**, then reload the window.

Requires VS Code 1.105 or newer. The packages are not code-signed. Full instructions: [install guide](https://github.com/b1tninja/continuous/blob/main/docs/continuous-install.md). Continuous is also on the VS Code Marketplace as **Continuous** (`b1tninja.continuous`).

| Platform                    | File                                                                       |
| --------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Windows x64 / Arm64         | `continuous-win32-x64-2.16.0.vsix`, `continuous-win32-arm64-2.16.0.vsix`   |
| macOS Apple Silicon / Intel | `continuous-darwin-arm64-2.16.0.vsix`, `continuous-darwin-x64-2.16.0.vsix` |
| Linux x64 / Arm64           | `continuous-linux-x64-2.16.0.vsix`, `continuous-linux-arm64-2.16.0.vsix`   |

Each platform also has an **agents** build, `continuous-<platform>-2.16.0-agents.vsix`. It adds Continuous to VS Code's Agents window through APIs that are still proposed, so it works in VS Code Insiders, or in Stable started with `code --enable-proposed-api b1tninja.continuous`. Without that it works like the normal build. See [VS Code Chat and Agents](https://b1tninja.github.io/continuous/customize/vscode-chat-and-agents).

## The CLI

The terminal agent is attached as `continuous-cli-2.16.0.tgz`. Install it on Node 22 or newer:

```sh
npm i -g https://github.com/b1tninja/continuous/releases/download/v2.16.0-vscode/continuous-cli-2.16.0.tgz
```

The package is `@b1tninja/continuous-cli` and the command is `continuous` (`continuous serve` is the headless server; the notes below call it `cn serve` where the docs do). The short command `cn` also works; both run the same program. It reads the same `~/.continuous` configuration as the extension.

## What's new since 2.14.0

**This release is mostly about doing what you chose and saying what it does.** At the top level of an area (now called IDGAF; a saved `yolo` still works) nothing asks any more, loops keep going when Plan edits and Questions are permissive, and file edits can reach outside the workspace. The terminal agent gets the hardened fetch the IDE uses, trust gates for `environment.json` and git-ai, and its root safety flags now reach `serve` and `acp`. Provider setup downloads model lists only when you ask. Loop mode's plan card becomes a collapsed tile with a to-do tree. Read Behaviour changes first: several defaults are stricter or looser than in 2.14.0.

### Behaviour changes

**The YOLO level is now IDGAF, and at IDGAF nothing asks.** (#687, #698, #699)

- At Questions IDGAF no question waits for you any more, outside a loop too. `cn`'s AskQuestion (terminal UI, `-p`, `serve`), a plan's decisions made in Plan mode, held questions left over when you move a loop to IDGAF, an item over its limit under Suggest and an MCP server's elicitation are all answered by the system. A call that a loop would hold for approval is refused instead of held, and a call at an IDGAF-level area that still asked (a command that hides what it runs) is refused with its reason.
- The answer is the option labelled `(recommended)`, else the plan's pick, else the first option, else "No one is available to answer; use your best judgment and state the assumption", recorded as `system` with `Questions: IDGAF` and shown as `Auto-answered: <question> -> <answer>`. Your own "you decide" list no longer applies at IDGAF. MCP elicitation takes the server's defaults, or is declined when a field has none or asks for a secret. Permissive, Automatic, Cautious and Manual are unchanged.

**Loop mode goes on when Plan edits and Questions are permissive.** (#674)

- A loop no longer stops on a plan card or in the Questions panel when you chose not to be asked. At Plan edits Automatic, Permissive or IDGAF a re-plan (a repair, a replaced check, added or dropped to-dos) is accepted and the next round starts. Before, a re-plan that replaced a failed item's check always waited, even at IDGAF.
- At Questions Automatic, Permissive or IDGAF a question the agent asks, and a decision in a plan, is answered by the system: the option labelled `(recommended)`, else the first, else "No one is available to answer; use your best judgment and state the assumption". The record says `system` and names the setting. At Manual and Cautious nothing changes.
- The loop panel shows one non-blocking line for each, such as `Plan updated: 11 kept, 1 added, 1 dropped; check of item 1 replaced` and `Auto-answered: <question> -> <answer>`. The extension, `cn` and `cn serve` share one rule. See "What Plan edits and Questions do for a loop" in the Permissions page docs.

**File edits at IDGAF reach outside the workspace.** (#691, shipped with #699)

At File edits = IDGAF (the top level, also reached by `--auto`), the agent can create, edit and write files outside the workspace folder, in the editor, the terminal UI, headless `-p` and `serve`, with no prompt and no refusal. Before, a headless run refused such a write whatever the level, and the editor's exact edit tools treated an absolute path elsewhere as a file that does not exist.

- Each such write is listed in the audit trail as allowed by the level, with the resolved absolute path, and the tool result says `Wrote outside the workspace: <path>`.
- Lower levels are unchanged: Manual, Cautious and Automatic ask, Permissive holds it by the outside-paths protection.
- Still binding at IDGAF: the locked policy files, a tool switched off, an organisation ceiling and the `floor:` rules you wrote. Secret-file name checks inside the file tools, and the webview's own write guard (used for plan files), are not changed.
- Separate fix: an absolute path inside the workspace given to the new-file tool is now written where it says, not under a folder named after the drive.

**Hub assistants and the generated SDK client are removed.** (#671)

- The generated hub/API SDK client (`packages/continue-sdk`) is deleted, together with the terminal agent's API client service and the `CONTINUE_API_BASE` setting. The code no longer names a Continue-operated host, and `core/egress/egress-allowlist.json` has no entry for one.
- `--config owner/slug` (a hub assistant) now fails with "hub assistants are not supported; pass a config.yaml path". Pass a path to a `config.yaml`.

**Other behaviour changes.** (#743, #735, #698)

- A root `--policy` or `--trust-project-hooks` now reaches `continuous serve` and `continuous acp` when it is written before the subcommand. Before, `continuous --policy careful serve` dropped the policy without a word and ran with the default one.
- The git-ai integration is now off by default. The terminal agent used to run `git-ai` (found through PATH, with the workspace as its working directory) around every file edit whenever it was installed. It now runs only if your own `settings.json` in your Continuous folder says `"gitAiIntegration": true`, and then only the `git-ai` found in an absolute PATH entry outside the workspace, by its full path. A project cannot switch it on.
- `continuous serve` no longer runs the `install` command from `.continuous/environment.json` or `.continue/environment.json` unless the folder is trusted. Run `continuous project trust` (or pass `--trust-project-config`) to keep the old behaviour; `serve` prints one line on stderr when it skips the file. Set `"environmentInstall": false` in your own `settings.json` to turn it off even for a trusted folder. See the workspace trust page.
- The YOLO level is now called IDGAF; existing settings keep working. A saved `yolo` (settings, loops, `--policy yolo`) is read as `idgaf`, and nothing writes the old name.
- **The terminal agent's `Fetch` tool now uses the same hardened fetch as the IDE.** It used to hand Node's global `fetch` to the shared implementation, which ignores the pinned address the safety check resolved (so a name that changed its answer between the check and the connection could reach a private address), your proxy, CA bundle, `verifySsl` and client certificate. It now goes through `@continuedev/fetch` with the pin and your `requestOptions` transport settings. Your `requestOptions.headers` are sent only to your configured models' hosts, never to a URL the model chose. If you relied on `Fetch` working without your proxy or CA settings, it will now use them.
- **A fetched page is labelled with the URL it was read from, not the one the model asked for.** After a redirect the item's name source, `uri` and the spotlight source name the final URL, so a page that redirected to another host says so. Redirects are still followed one hop at a time and still refused when they lead from a public address to a private one. Not changed: a redirect to a different public host does not ask for approval.

**Model lists are downloaded when you ask, not when a screen opens.** (#690)

- Provider setup no longer contacts `ollama.com` or `openrouter.ai` when it opens. Ollama asks "Download the latest model list from ollama.com?"; OpenRouter asks "Pull the latest model information from OpenRouter?" with **Pull now**, **Not now** and **Don't ask again** (saved as `modelCatalog: never` in `config.yaml`). **Refresh** stays on the model step.
- The OpenRouter list (names, context sizes, per-token prices) is kept on this computer, dated, in `model-catalog/openrouter.json` in the global folder, and read from there afterwards. If the site cannot be reached, the list you already had stays.
- The details are in [PRIVACY.md](https://github.com/b1tninja/continuous/blob/main/PRIVACY.md) and the OpenRouter provider page.

### New

- **Loop mode's plan card is a collapsed tile with a fold-away to-do tree** (title, plan file link, the round line and one root row; the done items fold away, the current item shows its live lines, a re-plan marks kept, added and dropped to-dos). Outside a loop the card is unchanged. (#694)
- **A calmer Loop mode.** Duplicated headings, pointers and usage lines are gone; the top-level warning is one chip in the mode bar; "Recently blocked" is a shield badge with a count; the config selector becomes an icon at narrow widths. (#688) The gradient loop frame component and its CLI colour map are added, not yet wired to the dock. (#683)
- **The approval row says what a pending tool call will do** (the command, the file or the address), not just the tool name and a cut-off policy note. (#673)
- **Choose a local model on the onboarding Local tab:** Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp, vLLM or any OpenAI-compatible server, with the server address, the installed Ollama models and the `ollama pull` command for one that is missing. (#692)
- **OpenRouter model information is asked for once and kept as a dated local copy.** (#690, see Behaviour changes)
- The install scripts (`install.sh`, `install.ps1`) install this fork's CLI, `@b1tninja/continuous-cli`, not the upstream `@continuedev/cli`. (#670)

### Fixes

- The IDE now reads `AGENT.md` and `CLAUDE.md` as agent files; only `AGENTS.md` was ever tried. (#736)
- `continuous plan build` honours `--config` and the other root flags and prints why it refused. (#672)
- Anthropic model lists are read page by page, so accounts with more than one page see every model; Anthropic `stop_reason` is mapped to the OpenAI-style finish reason (length, tool calls, content filter); a 404 for a retired model names its replacement. (#737)
- MCP servers on Windows started through `npx`, `uvx`, `bunx` and the like no longer have `& | ^ % < >` in their arguments read by `cmd.exe`; a server's stderr is capped (first and last 4 KiB) and masked before it is shown in a connect-failure message. (#738)
- The OpenAI adapters use `ai` 7 to match the `@ai-sdk/*` v4 providers, which fixes Anthropic through the AI SDK. (#741)
- Flaky `QueuedMessages` GUI tests made deterministic (#693); prettier on `plans/ROADMAP.md` (#760); the YOLO guard test allows the two reference pages that document the alias (#796).

### Docs

- New and corrected pages for the terminal agent, Loop mode and the CLI reference, checked against the code (#785); dead links, old folder names and the Marketplace statement fixed (#777); hook and prompt-injection pages corrected (#736); the IDGAF rename across docs and plans (#699).
- Research reports and roadmap updates, internal with no user-visible change: #669, #689, #702, #704 to #716, #718 to #733, #742, #748, #759, #761, #762, #764, #767, #768, #771, #773 to #776, #778, #779, #781, #782.
- Dependency updates: #657, #675, #676, #677, #678, #680, #682, #686.

### Upgrade notes

- A saved `yolo` level is read as `idgaf`; nothing to change. At IDGAF, questions are answered by the system and file edits can reach outside the workspace: pick Permissive if you want to be asked.
- `--config owner/slug` (a hub assistant) fails; pass a path to a `config.yaml`.
- To keep `continuous serve` running `environment.json`'s `install` command, trust the folder (`continuous project trust`). To keep git-ai, set `"gitAiIntegration": true` in your own `settings.json`.
- Provider setup asks before it downloads a model list; choose **Don't ask again** to save `modelCatalog: never`.

## Planning

[`plans/ROADMAP.md`](https://github.com/b1tninja/continuous/blob/main/plans/ROADMAP.md) records what is built and what is not.

## Not included

The JetBrains plugin and the hosted Continue Hub are not part of Continuous. Hub `uses: owner/name` blocks are not supported; configure models and blocks directly or with local file paths.
